briefs.source_chain: PJM and ERCOT both hit record peak demand, but only PJM saw prices spike (168/162 GW, beat 2006 record and forecast, >$2,000/MWh; smaller 159 GW peak >$1,000/MWh, forwards stayed strong) because ERCOT's 91 GW record was absorbed by renewables/storage (low-hundreds pricing) and its forwards have weakened further, especially after Abbott's letter paused Batch Zero, pushing the curve into contango; therefore MISO/NE/NY/CA came in mixed vs forecast, gas turbine orders hit a record 38 GW (+71% YoY, NA-led), and Wolfe holds sentiment flat at '2,' flagging the RBP cost-allocation item (mitigated by Wolfe's own read that cost falls on the customer and deals should stay intact) against improving CEG tone.
briefs.brief_chain: Same peaks-and-pricing chain (PJM record + price spike vs ERCOT record + no price reaction because renewables/storage absorbed it, ERCOT forwards weakening into contango post-Abbott letter) -> MISO/NY/CA line -> record gas turbine orders -> flat '2' sentiment, RBP-cost-allocation risk flagged pending FERC, CEG tone improving, Cogentrix cleared FERC.

distortions.what: Brief presents the PJM RBP cost-allocation item as simply 'a risk still pending FERC' and drops Wolfe's own mitigating read that the cost/curtailment burden falls on the customer, not the IPP, and that Wolfe expects the existing PPA deals to remain intact.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the source attaches no explicit buy/sell call to this line item, and the sector-wide sentiment meter the brief also reports (flat '2') is unchanged, so there is no trade to redirect.

distortions.what: Brief states 'Vistra's Cogentrix deal cleared FERC' alongside the sentiment-meter narrative, but that fact actually comes from a separate, later 'Pending' regulatory-chronology section of the document, not the sentiment-meter paragraph.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the fact itself is accurate and undisputed; only its place in the document is misattributed by juxtaposition.

distortions.what: Brief's 'elsewhere' line names only MISO/NY/CA and drops that New England was also down YoY but basically in-line with forecast.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — omitting one in-line region changes no directional read.
